card.name: Capoeira
card.era: Developed by enslaved Africans; first references early 19th century
card.profile: Capoeira is an Afro-Brazilian cultural practice that is simultaneously a fight and a dance, played by two people inside a circle (roda) while others sing, clap and play instruments such as the berimbau and atabaque. Movements require great bodily dexterity. Born of resistance among enslaved Africans, it spread worldwide. The Capoeira circle (Roda de Capoeira) was inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List in 2014 (file 00892, decision 9.COM 10.8); IPHAN registered it nationally in 2008 (UNESCO; Agencia Brasil).
card.insight: UNESCO inscribed the capoeira circle on 25 November 2014; the nomination was Brazil's only submission that year (UNESCO).
